家.meaning: A <part>pig</part> moves in under your <part>roof</part>, takes the best bed and refuses to leave. It even hangs up a picture of itself. Now it isn't just your place: it's the pig's <kanji>house</kanji> too.
家.on: The pig fills the bath and keeps a big orange <sound>car</sound>p in it.
家.kun: When you ask the pig to leave, it squeals '<sound>Ee</sound>-<sound>eh</sound>!' and burrows under the blanket.

路.meaning: A <part>foot</part> stomps across the grass, stopping at <part>each</part> house in turn to knock with its toe. House after house, step after step, it wears a line into the grass: a <kanji>path</kanji>.
路.on: A little <sound>ro</sound>dent scurries along the path too, squeaking at each turn.
路.kun: Then a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p bumps along the path and makes it even wider.

主.meaning: A <part>king</part> wears a <part>lid</part> for a crown, with a single knob on top bigger than any other king's jewel. When he enters the hall, every other king bows. He's the <kanji>lord</kanji> of them all.
主.on: At the feast, the lord takes all the <sound>su</sound>gar cubes for himself.
主.kun: At every meal the lord spots a mole in his soup: '<sound>Oh</sound>! <sound>Mo</sound>le!'

味.meaning: A <part>mouth</part> waits beside a young fruit tree that's <part>not yet</part> grown: one short new branch sits above the long one. The mouth can't wait and bites a hard green fruit. Sour, sharp, strange: a <kanji>flavor</kanji> it has never had.
味.on: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat pops up beside the mouth to taste the fruit too.
味.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>gee</sound>!' says the mouth, juice running down its chin, and reaches for another.

力.meaning: One stroke bends like an arm with the elbow out, and a second stroke crosses it like a bulging <part>muscle</part>. Make a fist, flex, and feel the <kanji>power</kanji>.
力.on: A trio of strongmen toast with <sound>Rio</sound>ja, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock falls off the shaking wall.
力.kun: A cheetah flexes and lifts a whole car over its head as the crowd cheers: '<sound>Chee</sound>! <sound>Kah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>!'

田.meaning: A square split into four smaller squares, like farmland seen from a plane, with paths running between the plots. Each plot is flooded with water and planted with green shoots: a <kanji>rice field</kanji>.
田.on: A <sound>den</sound>tist sets up a chair in the middle of the field and pulls teeth among the shoots.
田.kun: The farmer shows off the four neat plots with a bow: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!'

男.meaning: A farmer heaves a whole <part>rice field</part> over his head, his <part>muscle</part> bulging underneath it. Mud drips down his arms. That field-lifter, in this kanji, is the <kanji>male</kanji>.
男.on: Under the lifted field is a dripping <sound>dun</sound>geon, and its prisoners blink up at the daylight.
男.kun: He drops the field on a totem pole. '<sound>Oh</sound>!' he gasps as the <sound>to</sound>tem wobbles and a <sound>ko</sound>ala tumbles off the top.
